correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge3\), the ray differences \(v_{p,q}-v_{p,r}=e_r-e_q\) generate \(N\). Upper-facet Cartier linearity gives a three-index identity, then four-point additivity of symmetric edge weights, forcing every rational Cartier coefficient array to be a character plus a constant. Integral coefficients give \(u\in M\) and \(t\in\mathbb Z\). The two facet types require respectively \(2\mid t\) and \((2n-1)\mid t\). Hence \(\operatorname{Pic}(X_n)=\mathbb Z[-(4n-2)K_{X_n}]\). Saturation of \(M+\mathbb Z\mathbf1\) within the full ray-coefficient lattice proves that the anticanonical class is primitive in \(\operatorname{Cl}(X_n)\). The uniform proof includes the \(n=3\) boundary; exact finite-rank checks for \(3\le n\le6\) corroborate, but do not replace, the argument.

value.rationale: The family is a distinguished recent K-polystable Q-Fano example at small alpha. The new global Cartier rigidity shows Picard rank 1 versus Weil rank \(n^2\) and computes the exact primitive ample polarization and finite-plus-free divisor obstruction. These integral global invariants are geometrically motivated by line bundles and non-Q-factoriality and are not supplied by local fixed-point calculations. The result is a complete natural infinite-family classification rather than a routine reparameterization.
